identity_marker: black Nikon D850 camera body with textured grips and a matte black 85mm lens

video_goal: Demonstrate the physical steps to configure a Nikon D850 camera for portrait photography, focusing on exposure and autofocus settings.
single_prompt: A close-up side view reveals the black Nikon D850 camera body with textured grips and a matte black 85mm lens set against a softly lit, neutral gray studio background with warm overhead continuous lighting. Hands align the white dot on the base of the portrait lens with the white dot on the camera mount, twisting the lens counter-clockwise until it audibly clicks into place. The camera smoothly transitions to an extreme close-up top-down view as a finger flicks the power switch collar surrounding the shutter button on the top right of the camera body to the 'ON' position. Transitioning to an over-the-shoulder top-down view, a finger presses and holds the 'MODE' button on the top-left dial cluster while a thumb rotates the rear main command dial until the letter 'M' appears on the top LCD screen. In a close-up top-down view, an index finger rotates the front sub-command dial, rapidly changing the aperture value on the top LCD screen until it stops at 'f/1.8'. Still in a close-up top-down view, a thumb rotates the rear main command dial, changing the shutter speed value on the top LCD screen until it reads '200'. Next, a finger presses the 'ISO' button located just behind the shutter button and rotates the rear dial until the number '100' is displayed on the top LCD screen. The view smoothly transitions to a close-up front-left view as a finger presses and holds the AF-mode button located on the lower-left front of the D850 body, right next to the lens mount. Shifting back to an over-the-shoulder top-down view, while holding the AF-mode button, a thumb rotates the rear main command dial until the text 'AF-S' appears on the top LCD screen. Still holding the AF-mode button, an index finger rotates the front sub-command dial until a single small square icon for Single-point AF appears on the top LCD screen. The camera angle moves to an over-the-shoulder rear view as a finger presses the 'Lv' Live View button on the back right of the camera body, activating the large rear LCD screen to reveal a live feed of a portrait model. In a close-up rear view, a finger taps the rear touchscreen directly over the model's right eye, causing a small red focus box to instantly move to that exact spot on the screen. Finally, an index finger half-presses the shutter button, turning the red focus box on the rear LCD screen green, accompanied by a brief visual confirmation of sharp focus on the model's eye.
